title: Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics
subtitle: A rigorous introduction to the fundamentals of CFD, from basic numerical discretisation to the solution of the full Navier–Stokes equations, with equal weight on the theory (stability, consistency, convergence) and on writing the schemes yourself.
startNote: Next offered as an elective in Jan–May 2027. The syllabus and assessment shown here are those of the Jan–May 2026 offering; details for 2027 will be posted at the start of term.
modulesLead: Five modules, moving from the building blocks of numerical methods to grids and applications.

modules.title: Fundamentals of numerical methods
items: Digital computing: machine epsilon, round-off errors
Classification of PDEs: elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic
Physical behaviour: advection and diffusion equations

modules.title: Hyperbolic equations — the wave equation
items: Discretisation schemes for the 1D first-order wave equation
Systems of equations: quasi-1D Euler and full Euler equations

modules.title: Parabolic equations — the heat equation
items: Multi-dimensional problems: alternating direction implicit (ADI) method

modules.title: Elliptic equations — Laplace & Poisson
items: Point iterative techniques: Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel, SOR

modules.title: Grid generation & applications
items: Transformation of equations to curvilinear coordinates

assessmentLead: Continuous assessment, as run in Jan–May 2026. Coding is a mandatory component.

assessment.d: Four assignments, 10% each — derivations and basic coding (e.g. 1D solvers)
Four 15-minute quizzes, 5% each, based on case studies shared with the class
Term project on a chosen track (beginner / intermediate / advanced) + written exam based on the project

rules: Coding is mandatory — every scheme studied is also implemented.
The capstone uses a tiered project system: choose a beginner, intermediate or advanced track.
Projects reproduce specific historical results (e.g. Chorin 1967, Sod 1978).
Code copied from elsewhere, or AI-generated without understanding, fails the project component.

references.text: Anderson, J. D. — Computational Fluid Dynamics: The Basics with Applications, McGraw-Hill.
Tannehill, J. C., Anderson, D. A. & Pletcher, R. H. — Computational Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer, Taylor & Francis.
Ramakrishna, M. — Elements of Computational Fluid Dynamics.
Ferziger, J. H. & Perić, M. — Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics, Springer.
Toro, E. F. — Riemann Solvers and Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics, Springer, 2009.
